This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though appeal is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken-up for final disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 12.02.2018 passed by II Addl. District and Sessions Court and Addl. MACT, Bidar sitting at Basavakalyan (for short 'tribunal') in MVC No.112/2017, this appeal is filed.
3.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Sanjeevkumar C. Patil, learned counsel for appellants submitted that appeal was by claimants for NC: 2023:KHC-K:7488 enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that since insurer had not preferred appeal, finding of tribunal about occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle due to its rash and negligent driving, causing death in said accident, issuance of insurance policy and its coverage as on date of accident were not in dispute.
Hanmanthappa And Ors vs Anuradha And Anr on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44028705/
2 4.

entities.text: Hanmanthappa And Ors vs Anuradha And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was submitted that as on date of accident i.e. 10.10.2016, Santosh was aged 27 years, working as mason and earning `24,000/- per month.
However, tribunal erroneously considered his monthly income at `7,000/-.
It also failed to add future prospects and even award under conventional heads was meager.
On above grounds, sought for enhancement of compensation.
5. On other hand, Shri S.S.Aspalli, learned counsel for respondent no.2/insurer sought to support award.
It was submitted that tribunal had awarded excessive rate of interest which would off-set scope for enhancement and sought dismissal of appeal.
Heard learned counsel for parties.

Perused impugned judgment and award.
7. From above submission and since only claimants are in appeal for enhancement, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation ?"
8. Though claimants stated that deceased was earning `24,000/- per month as mason, same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, tribunal assessed it notionally.
But, notional income for year 2016 adopted for settlement of cases before Lok-Adalat is `8,750/-.
Therefore, same has to be considered.
9. Deceased was self employed bachelor below 40 years and claimants are parents and siblings.

As per ratio laid down in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1, claimants would be entitled for addition of '40%' towards future prospects, deduction (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC:
2023:KHC-K:7488 towards personal expenses has to be at '' and multiplier applicable would be '17'.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, compensation under 'loss of dependency' would be :
(`8,750 + 40% - ) X 12 X 17 =`12,49,500/-.
10.

As per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs.
Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others2, claimants no.1 and 2 being parents would be entitled to `40,000/- each towards loss of 'parental consortium'.
11.

entities.text:
Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs.
Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In addition, they would be entitled for `15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses' and `15,000/-
towards 'loss of estate'.
And since more than three years have lapsed after rendering of decision in Pranay Sethi's case (supra), they would be entitled for addition of 10% to award under conventional heads (i.e. `11,000/-).
Thus total compensation would be `13,70,500/-.

In view of ratio laid down by this Court in case of Shriram General Insurance Company Limited,
Rajasthan vs. Smt.Laxmi and others3, rate of interest will have to be at 6%.

sentences.text: 3 ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part with costs.
(ii) Claimants are held entitled for total compensation of `13,70,500/- as against `7,84,000/- awarded by tribunal.
Thus there is enhancement of `5,86,500/- which shall carry interest at 6% p.a. from date of petition till deposit.
(iii) Respondent no.2/Insurer is directed to deposit it within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.

(iv) On deposit, claimant no.1 is held entitled for lump-sum amount of `1,50,000/-,
which shall be released to him and entire remaining amount is apportioned in favour of claimant no.2, which shall be kept in fixed deposit in 2018 (4) AKR 808 NC:
2023:KHC-K:7488 any Nationalized Bank or Postal Deposits as per choice of claimant for period of five years initially, with liberty to withdraw interest accrued thereon periodically.
